operator_evidence: AAR Appendix A: NORDUnet interface flapping reported at 15:33 (INC0040272); customer disabled the interface at 16:50 to regain stability; availability window 16:50-21:33 (INC0040289); interface re-enabled at 20:48.
bgp_observation: 11 of 33 selected observer-prefix streams (all AS2603 via AS11537) became absent at 16:45:25Z and returned at 16:45:27Z (2 s); 30 path replacements followed (16:45:26-17:02:03Z), with 11 streams departing the reviewed transit and 11 retaining it with material path changes; all 33 streams returned to baseline paths by 17:02:19Z.
temporal_relationship: Before { duration: 4 minutes 35 seconds } — first BGP absence 16:45:25Z precedes the reported 16:50 interface-disable action
interpretation: Public BGP showed transient route-state changes for the selected NORDUnet streams during the broader operator-reported instability period. The first selected stream absence occurred at 16:45:25Z, approximately 4 minutes 35 seconds before the AAR's reported 16:50 interface-disable action. The selected routes returned to baseline by 17:02:19Z, well before the reported 20:48 re-enable. The observation is therefore not attributed specifically to either interface action; temporal association with the broader instability interval is the supported reading.
limitation: One selected public collector (route-views2, single peer 64.57.28.241); a 2-second absence at one observer may reflect session behavior rather than the participant's own action; Layer-2 replication and the interface command are not observable in public BGP.
finding: Public BGP exposed a temporally related routing consequence for one reviewed participant (NORDUnet, AS2603) at one selected public collector during the reported incident — transient route-state disruption temporally associated with the broader reported instability interval, not attributed to either specific interface action. Single-target, single-collector, single-window pilot; not a complete MAN LAN incident verdict.
